Arrayed
a-RAYD
verb (past tense), adjective
From the Old French arreer, to put in order, and that from a Late Latin compound of ad and a Germanic root meaning to make ready — whence also array, the ordered ranks of an army. To array is to clothe in order and dignity, not merely to cover.

Biblical Definition

To be arrayed is to be clothed by another’s hand, and Scripture makes the arraying a matter of who does the clothing. Pharaoh “arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck” (Gen 41:42), and Joseph goes from the dungeon to the second chariot in a single verse; the robe is the visible token of an office he did not seize. Haman is compelled to array Mordecai and lead his horse through the street (Est 6:11), which is one of the sharpest reversals in Scripture — the man who built the gallows dresses the man he meant to hang. Our Lord uses the word to end all anxiety about clothing: “even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these” (Mat 6:29). The lily is better dressed than the richest king in Israel’s history, and it neither toils nor spins; therefore the God who arrays a flower for a day will not neglect His children. And the word reaches its end in the marriage of the Lamb, where the bride is “arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints” (Rev 19:8) — and the text carefully says it was granted to her. Even the white she wears at the wedding is a gift. From Joseph to the bride, no one in Scripture arrays himself.

Webster 1828 Definition

Clothed, dressed, or adorned, especially with dignity or in order; also, drawn up in ranks. In Scripture, always the clothing put on by another’s hand.

expand to see more

ARRAY, v.t. To place or dispose in order, as troops for battle.

To deck or dress; to adorn with dress; applied especially to rich or splendid garments.

From the Old French arreer, to put in order, to make ready.

ARRAYED, pp. Clothed; adorned; drawn up in order.

In law, to set a jury in order for the trial of a cause.

Key Scripture

Gen 41:42 — "And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;"

Est 6:11 — "Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour."

Mat 6:29 — "And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these."

Rev 19:8 — "And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints."

Modern Corruption

The self-made man is the age’s ideal, and he is precisely the man Scripture never shows — every arraying in the Bible is done by a hand other than the wearer’s.

expand to see more

The corruption is self-investiture. The reigning story of our time is the one in which a man rises by his own effort, robes himself in an honour he has earned, and owes the credit to nobody. Scripture tells no such story. Joseph is arrayed by Pharaoh, Mordecai by Haman’s unwilling hands, the lilies by God, the bride by grant. Even the high priest was washed and clothed by Moses at his consecration; he did not vest himself. The pattern is so consistent that it amounts to a doctrine: honour is conferred, never assumed, and the man who dresses himself in a dignity no one gave him is an impostor however fine the cloth.

Recover the plain sense: the doctrine of imputed righteousness stands or falls here. Rev 19:8 says the bride’s fine linen is the righteousness of saints, and in the same breath that it was granted to her — the works are truly hers and the ability to do them was given. Set that against the filthy rags of Isa 64:6 and the wedding garment of Mat 22:11, where a man is cast out for attending in his own clothes. The gospel does not ask a sinner to improve his wardrobe. It strips him and arrays him, and the shame of the stripping is the price of the robe. Mat 6:29 then applies the comfort at the humblest level: a Father who dresses grass will dress you.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old French arreer, to set in order — clothing conferred by another’s hand, never assumed by the wearer.

expand to see more

Arrayed — Old French arreer, to put in order, make ready.

The same word gives the military array, ranks set in order.

Gen 41:42: the robe is the token of a conferred office.

Mat 6:29: the lily outdresses Solomon without toiling or spinning.

Rev 19:8: the bride’s linen is hers, and was granted to her.

Usage

"No one in Scripture arrays himself — the hand is always another’s."

"Est 6:11: Haman must array the man he built a gallows for."

"Rev 19:8 holds imputed righteousness and real works together in one verse."
